threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, governance, and overall rollout plan for the quality system.

messages.text: Hi team, kicking off the Cross-site Quality Management System Rollout project. I've created the initial draft of the framework document, please see A1. It outlines the proposed governance model and principles. Your feedback is welcome as we get started on T1 and T4.

Thanks for sharing. I'm reading through A1 now. I have a question on the governance section - it defines roles for the central quality team and site supervisors, but the interaction model isn't fully clear. How do we ensure feedback from sites is incorporated into the central framework over time?
Good question. The intention is that site supervisors handle local day-to-day issues, and anything systemic gets escalated to the central team for a decision.

That makes sense for escalations. I'd also suggest we build in a formal quarterly review where supervisors can present suggestions for improvement. It would make the governance feel more collaborative and help us catch small issues before they become systemic.
I like that. A proactive feedback loop. Let's add a 'Quarterly Governance Review' to the model in A1. I'll make that update.
Great. Moving on to the scope for T2, the process mapping. What's the basis for the initial list of processes we need to map?
I started with a list of the most frequently used processes from the existing site-level documentation.

That's a reasonable starting point. To ensure we're focusing on what matters most for compliance, I suggest we prioritize the processes that have the highest risk profile based on our last internal audit cycle. That will ensure our efforts in T2 directly support risk mitigation.
Excellent point. A risk-based approach is much stronger. Let's pivot to that. Okay, let's lock in these first two key decisions.
Decision 1: We will approve the quality management framework and governance model as defined in A1, with the addition of a quarterly feedback review session. Do we agree?
Yes, agreed.
Decision 2: For the first wave of the rollout, we will confirm the list of key processes for T2 based on the highest-risk items from the last audit cycle. Agreed?
Agreed. I can pull that list from the audit reports and have it ready by tomorrow morning.

Perfect. To summarize: D1 and D2 are confirmed. I will update A1 today. @436982 you will provide the high-risk process list tomorrow to kick off T2. I will continue building out the detailed project plan in T4.

threads.thread_goal: Converge on standardized SOPs and risk/compliance approach.

messages.text: Hi team, as part of T3, I've drafted the first batch of Standardized SOPs for the high-risk processes we identified. They are now available in the A2 document pack for review. I've also started the risk assessment for T8 and have a few initial items in A6.
Thanks @436982, great progress. I'm reviewing A2 now.

The content of the SOPs looks thorough. My main feedback is on the format. It's quite detailed, which is good for auditors, but might be a bit much for operators on the floor. Could we create a simpler template, maybe with more visuals or a summary box at the top?

That's a fair point. We need the detail for compliance, but usability is key for adoption. How about this: we establish a standard SOP template that includes a mandatory 'Key Steps & Summary' section on the first page. This gives operators a quick reference, while the full details remain for deep dives and audits.
A standard template with a summary section is a great compromise. Let's make that official. What about the approval workflow for these?
I'd propose a simple workflow: I draft the SOP, you review it from a project perspective, and then it goes to the Compliance Officer for final sign-off before publishing.

That works. It's clear and covers our bases. Okay, let's lock that in. Decision: We agree on a final SOP template that includes a summary section, and an approval workflow of QE Draft -> PM Review -> Compliance Sign-off. Sound good?
Yes, confirmed. I'll update the documents in A2 to reflect this new template.
Now, for the risk register in A6. As I populate it during T8, we need a consistent way to prioritize the risks. I assume we'll use an Impact and Likelihood matrix?
Yes, a standard High/Medium/Low matrix for Impact and Likelihood should work. We can focus on anything that comes out as High-High.

That's a good start. For our context, especially with compliance, we might benefit from adding a 'Detectability' score. A high-impact risk that's hard to detect is often more dangerous than one that's obvious. We could calculate a Risk Priority Number (RPN) from all three factors to get a more nuanced priority list.
You're right, RPN is a much more robust method. I'd forgotten about that. Let's definitely use that. It will make our conversations with stakeholders much clearer.

Okay, second decision for this thread: For risk prioritization in A6, we will use criteria based on Impact, Likelihood, and Detectability to calculate a Risk Priority Number (RPN). We'll prioritize mitigation actions for the highest RPN scores. Agreed?
Agreed. That gives me a clear framework for T8. I'll structure the A6 register with columns for I, L, D, and the calculated RPN.
Excellent. So, next steps: @436982 you'll update the SOP template in A2 and set up the risk register A6 with the RPN structure. I'll start scheduling the reviews with Compliance for the first SOPs.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in KPI set, targets, and reporting cadence for the dashboard.

messages.text: Hi all, for T5, I have drafted the Quality KPI Dictionary and a mock-up of the dashboard. Please see A3 for the details. I'd like to get your feedback on the proposed KPIs and reporting structure before we start the build for T10.

Thanks, reviewing A3 now. The list of KPIs seems to cover the key areas. I do have a question about the definition for 'First Pass Yield'. It's a critical metric, but sites often measure it differently. We need to be very specific on whether this is pre- or post-rework to ensure we get clean, comparable data.
That's a very good point. I hadn't specified that. What is the standard best practice here?

The standard approach is to measure it before any form of rework or repair. This gives a true picture of the initial quality of the process. I can add a precise, unambiguous definition to the dictionary in A3.
Please do. That clarity is essential. With that clarification, are we happy to lock in this list of 5 core KPIs for our cross-site reporting? This would be our decision D5.
Yes, the other definitions are clear. This is a strong, manageable set of core KPIs to start with. I agree.
Great. Now for the reporting cadence and owners, also in A3. I've proposed that site supervisors own the data entry and that all KPIs are reported weekly. Any concerns?

Weekly cadence and supervisor ownership make sense for operational metrics. My only thought is on 'Customer Complaints'. That data can be laggy and sporadic. A weekly report might jump around a lot. Would a monthly reporting cycle for that specific KPI be more stable and meaningful?

I'd prefer to keep the reporting action consistent for the supervisors - one time a week for everything. What if we still have them enter the data weekly, but on the dashboard we display it as a month-to-date figure? That way the action is simple, but the view is stable.
That's a good solution. It balances simplicity for the data owners with a stable view for management. I can add that display logic to the dashboard spec for T10.

Perfect. Let's lock that in as D6: We confirm a weekly reporting cadence with site supervisors as data owners for all KPIs. The 'Customer Complaints' KPI will be displayed as a month-to-date value. Agreed?
Agreed.
Excellent. D5 and D6 are now closed. @436982 please update A3 with the FPY definition and the display logic for complaints. I will finalize the targets with the Operations Manager this week.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on training approach, schedule, and pilot site for the rollout.

messages.text: Hi team, I've completed the draft for the training curriculum and delivery guide (A4) as part of T6. It outlines the asynchronous modules and learning objectives. The document also includes a proposal for the pilot site to test our approach before the full rollout (related to T7). Feedback is welcome.
Thanks @436982, this is a critical piece. I'm reviewing A4 now.

The curriculum content looks great and covers all the new SOPs. I'm looking at the proposed schedule for T9 - you've allocated two weeks for all staff to complete the training. Given the different shift patterns across sites, do you think that's enough time?

That's a valid point. The two-week window is for the self-paced modules. To support this, I've also planned to run optional, live Q&A sessions with supervisors each week. We can also monitor completion rates daily and have managers follow up directly with anyone falling behind. This should provide the flexibility and support needed.

Okay, the combination of self-paced learning with live support and active tracking sounds robust. I'm comfortable with that approach. Shall we formally approve the training curriculum and high-level schedule as laid out in A4?
Yes, I'm ready for approval on my end. I can then start building out the final training materials.
Great, D8 is approved. Now, let's discuss the pilot for T7. You've proposed Site B. Can you share your reasoning?

I chose Site B because their operational profile includes a good mix of the high-risk processes we've standardized. Also, their site supervisor has been highly engaged in this initiative from the start, so I expect we'll get high-quality, constructive feedback from their team, which we can log in A7.
An engaged local champion is a huge advantage. I agree with the choice. What would we define as the success criteria for this pilot?

I'd propose three clear criteria: 1. At least 95% of the pilot team completes the training before go-live. 2. No P1 or P2 operational incidents related to the new processes in the first week. 3. We capture a minimum of 10 actionable feedback items in the A7 feedback log.
Those are clear, measurable, and directly tied to our project goals. I fully support them. Let's make it official.

Decision D7: We will select Site B for the pilot rollout, and we will measure its success based on the three criteria just defined (95% training completion, no major incidents, 10+ feedback items). Are we agreed?
Yes, agreed.

Fantastic. D7 and D8 are locked. I will communicate with the Site B leadership to formalize the pilot plan for T7. @436982 you can proceed with building the final training content for T6 and preparing for the broader rollout in T9.

threads.thread_goal: Review early results post-go-live and prioritize improvement backlog.

messages.text: Team, we've officially completed the first month since the full rollout. Great work getting us here! As part of T11, I've compiled a post-rollout review in A8, which includes our initial KPI performance and an improvement backlog based on site feedback. Please take a look.
Thanks for putting this together. It's great to see the data coming in. I'm reading through A8 now.

The good news is that most KPIs are trending positively. However, I've noticed a recurring issue logged in A8: 'Incorrect Form Usage' seems to be a common, low-level error at two sites. Any initial thoughts on a root cause?

I saw that too and reached out to one of the supervisors. It turns out the main link on their local intranet page was still pointing to an old version of the form. The SOP itself is correct, but their shortcut wasn't updated. It's likely the same issue at the other site.
Ah, a classic broken link problem. That's an easy fix. Can you coordinate with the site admins to get those updated?

I'm already on it. This also suggests an improvement for our process. I think we should update the Site Supervisor Checklist (A5) to include a pre-go-live step to 'Validate all local intranet links to quality documents'.
That's a great idea for preventing this in the future. Let's add that to the improvement backlog.

Speaking of checklists, I'm working on the quick-reference guide for supervisors (T12). Looking at the feedback in A8 and our risk register (A6), it seems there's still some minor confusion on the precise KPI definitions. I think it would be valuable to add a one-line definition for each KPI directly onto that checklist.
Yes, absolutely. Reinforcing the definitions at the point of use is a smart move. Please add that to the scope for T12.

Okay, looking at the full improvement backlog in A8, let's agree on priorities. I propose we prioritize items related to documentation clarity and data accuracy first. That would include the three items we just discussed.
I agree. Those will have the biggest impact on sustaining the improvements. Items like 'adding new optional fields to forms' can wait for the next cycle.

Perfect. So, to summarize the next steps from T11: our top priority improvements are fixing the broken links, updating the A5 checklist, and adding KPI definitions to the T12 guide. I will formalize this priority list in A8.
Sounds good. I can take ownership of getting those three actions completed.
